name: Rowan Kelly
home: a boat at South Shore Harbor
life: “I still remember my first night at sea without a shore address.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Rowan by a small Monday habit. Rowan pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I budgeted for timber and forgot the cost of a bed. I haven't rented a room since my marriage broke up.
appearance: Rowan is easy to recognize by a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears and a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread, Rowan draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first when listening.
personality: Rowan never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Rowan can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To find a bed for the dry-dock weeks.
family: Darcy Reyes is Rowan’s younger cousin. Rowan chooses the music. Darcy puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The trust with a typo*, Darcy says, “I asked the school to use my own nickname on the shortlist.”
connections: Grey Clement. The old berth lease may give the displaced resident a real key ashore. Also in the story is Drew Hayward (shore room coordinator).

reactions.situation: A yard manager asks the liveaboard to leave by Friday
reactions.response: Rowan asks where the resident can sleep on the first night ashore.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Rowan asks the stranger who will be expecting them, then helps find a way to tell that person.

reactions.situation: When a relative hints at needing company
reactions.response: Rowan may initially offer a repair, but sits down as soon as the request becomes clear.
